blog.title: v0.6.0 Beta — the biggest update yet
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: The biggest update yet, and possibly ever: recipes, send-to-OPNduck, AI chat and tools, colour grading, background removal, dubbing, a server, an Android app and a macOS beta. It might be super buggy.
blog.body:
This is the biggest update OPNduck has had, and possibly will ever have, and it might be super buggy. Please report what breaks.
New: Recipes (chain tools into one-click pipelines), Send to OPNduck (links from your phone, browser or another PC, end-to-end encrypted), Colour Grade, Background Remover, Beat Finder, Dubbing (Beta, local voice, no cloning), an AI chat that can propose jobs and run them after you confirm, search of the spoken words in your videos, summaries, chapters, a thumbnail picker, and a small local AI model of its own.
Also new: OPNduck Server (run jobs on another machine, also as a Docker image), an Android app, a macOS beta (Apple silicon, not notarized) and per-device access when you share your engine.
The Windows builds were made from Linux and have not been tried on real Windows. macOS and Android are unsigned. Full notes are on the GitHub release.

blog.title: v0.5.3 Beta — OPNduck in your terminal
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: A terminal version of OPNduck (also on npm) that uses about 100 MB instead of about 680 MB, plus a first-launch setup wizard that lets you pick what to install.
blog.body:
New: OPNduck TUI. All eight tools in a terminal with forms, path completion, live progress, a queue, library, settings and all the themes. It shares settings and history with the desktop app. Install with npm i -g opnduck-tui (needs Node.js 20 or newer) or unpack the tarball from the release.
New: a setup wizard on first launch (and in Settings, System) that lists the downloader, the fast video engine, Audio AI and Subtitles with their sizes and installs what you tick.
Under the hood the job code moved into Electron-free modules; the desktop app behaves the same.
The Tauri migration is still postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.

blog.title: v0.5.2 Beta — a calmer, pixel-style look
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: Home is a compact grid of tool tiles, there is a themed startup screen, a pixel wordmark, sharper corners, calmer colours and readable text in every theme.
blog.body:
Home now shows a small tile for each tool and opens only the one you pick, so the page is no longer crowded.
A new startup screen with a bobbing duck follows the theme you chose. The wordmark and a faint scatter of pixels give the app a blocky pixel look.
Colours are calmer (orange only for actions and the active item), corners are sharper, and dim text and icons are now readable in every Omarchy palette.
Engine checks are remembered between launches, so cards load faster, and there are more developer tools.
The Tauri migration is still postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.

blog.title: v0.5.1 Beta — AI apps can drive OPNduck
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: An optional local MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other AI apps start and watch OPNduck jobs. Plus animated menu icons and a few things to find.
blog.body:
A new optional MCP server (off by default, Settings → System) lets any MCP-capable AI app start downloads, conversions, upscales, trims and subtitles, watch progress and cancel jobs. It only listens on your own computer, needs a private token, and saves only to your download folder.
The menu icons now animate: the gear spins, the plug sparks, the books get pulled out, the house hops.
There is also something hiding for the curious.

blog.title: v0.5.0 Beta — the performance update
blog.author: Ducky
blog.excerpt: A faster GPU video engine (PyTorch streaming + NVENC), a trimmer with a visual editor, queue controls, watch folder, notifications, live logs on every card, Electron 45 and 24 new Omarchy palettes.
blog.body:
Video upscaling can now stream frames straight through the GPU and encode with NVENC: 1.4x to 3.6x faster end to end in my tests, depending on scale.
Long videos are processed in chunks so temp disk use stays small.
New: trimmer with a visual editor, pause/resume queue, parallel job limits, watch folder, finish notifications and tray mode, live logs on every card and a progress bar that only moves forward.
The Tauri migration is postponed: WebKitGTK stutters and crashes on NVIDIA + Wayland, so OPNduck stays on Electron for now.
